items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you ever hear Joe Oliver? [INTERVIEWEE] No.

ctx.x: Well, you might tell some of the early bands you played with when you left the, the shows. When did you come to New Orleans, Billy?

Well, I came to New Orleans and, I made it, my first trip to New Orleans, that's when my sister Sadie were here. She was playing on Steamer Madison Boat. That's when her and, uh, her first husband was together. Bebe Chani. Oh, yeah. Drummer. Well, she taken sick, well, I was, I was playing with the Nighthawk Orchestra band in Birmingham. So, after she told me she was sick, I left Birmingham and came to New Orleans. That's when my first trip. See? And, uh, well, I was, went to work on the boat in her place. So she…
Yeah. He played trumpet or what did he play?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ... Joe Oliver. Well, I even knew this fellow that you had mentioned. He's got a P.T. Buddy P.T. Buddy P.T. Yeah, I knew them too. Emmanuel Paris.

ctx.x: Oh, they got some wonderful people in this business.

I know so well. Steal everything they get a hold of. I know. Steal everything they get a hold of. I know. They had it under the table. Yeah, they just steal all my stuff. I wish we could do that. And if I know, see, by my back with 200 orange, I couldn't see, you know, looking like that all the time. And Joe, I see them. Joe, I see them. Joe, I see them. He said, business, I'm probably stealing. So I said, look on the table. I got up. I went to them. I went to them. Yeah, you're going to tell them about that.…
I will. Maybe we ought to get a little, uh, earnest on here too. Let's give it, let's give him a chance. Yeah, go ahead.
